messages.subject: 4-armed bandit task
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am currently working on a 4-armed restless bandit task, similar to that of Maarten & Konstanidis (2015 <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25899069/>). The task has 4 arms and the participant is expected to maximize their cumulative reward in a limited number of trials. In each trial, the participant clicks on one arm and the underlying reward is revealed.

I am trying a couple of 4-armed bandit fitting techniques available in hBayesDM. But I am not sure what exactly the required data columns mean, more specifically, 'gain' and 'loss'. In my task, the reward can be positive or negative. What I have been doing until now is that if a participant earns 40 reward points in a particular trial, then I enlist it under 'gain' for that trial and put zero in 'loss'. And similarly, if they earn -40, I enlist it as -40 under 'loss' and put zero in 'gain'. I would like to confirm if that's the correct way to interpret 'gain' and 'loss' for my task.
On the other hand, if I put all the rewards, positive and negative, under 'gain' (or 'loss') and put 'loss' (or 'gain') as zero, how do I interpret the result? Shall it give me the parameters I require but with no separate sensitivity to gains and losses.

Sorry to have written a long message, but any help would be appreciated.

Thanks in advance!
Pratham Shukla

messages.subject: Bart_par4 with two balloon colors
messages.body_plain:
Hey everyone,

I have a question about the bart_par4 model, in case anyone has come across a similar issue. We're using the version of the BART performed during fMRI with two different color balloons (blue and red) as well as white control balloons. The rewards for the red and blue balloons are associated with slightly different probability distributions (1/8 and 1/12). The bart_par4 model was designed on the original (one-balloon) task. Has anyone else thought about how to run the model for the two-balloon task?

So far, I ran the model with our data as is, as well as separating the blue and red balloons and running the model on each color separately. I've thought about modifying the model but wasn't sure if I should do something to account for the two different distributions since they are not completely independent.

If anyone has thought about this or has any ideas, I would really appreciate it. Thank you!
